transcript: Interview Guide. Activity E. FGD:  Aspirations of Youth
Module 1:  Agency, education and innovation (1 hour)

Position of the majority of young [sex of FGD] on the ladder of power and freedom (private rating) – Today: 5 = Power and freedom to make almost all major life decisions: 0 votes; 4 = Power and freedom to make many major life decisions: 0 votes; 3 = Power and freedom to make some major life decisions: 3 votes; 2 = Only a small amount of power and freedom: 3 votes; 1 = Almost no power or freedom to make decisions: 2 votes
Most of us are on the 3rd step of the ladder today; we have relatively more freedom today to take some important decisions of our lives
10 years back girls had no say in anything; not even those related to their lives
This is because we are going to school and parents are willing to educate us; before they never treated us at par with the boys
Now sons and daughters are meted out equal treatment
Before girls were not even allowed to step out of their home
This was because that girls should only stay confined to their home and do household chores
Before girls use to be married off at very tender age; now there is more awareness on this issue
Now girls are beings sent to school; before no one bothered to listen to us
It is very important that we girls also study
If children study then they learn lots of good things including good behaviour and that we should respect our elders
We will not fight and abuse each other if we go to school because we learn so many good things at school
Education is important if we want to move ahead in our lives
Education is important and should be an integral part of our lives
Boys are allowed to study as much as they want to
Boys study till 12th and even bachelors if they want to; girls are allowed to study only till 10th
75% of the boys who graduate (bachelors) are able to find jobs; the maximum a girl can study, if she insists, is till 12th
Boys are never asked to drop out of school or college

The difference in the different levels of education that parents allow their sons and daughters is primarily because by the time a girl passes class 12th she is 19-20 years old and the community starts pressurising her parents to marry her; so parents get her married
So once we get married our education is discontinued
Parents marry their daughters early to ease their own tension
Why the difference? We should also be allowed to study as much as we want
Yes, we should also complete graduation
Till daughters stay at home with their parents, parents treat them at par with their sons
Once we get married they don’t bother about us anymore
They care more for their sons
They think why educate their daughters when they have to go to someone else’s home post marriage
They think they must educate their sons else he will go wayward and become a goonda (bad man)
Sons’ education is always given more importance
They educate their sons thinking that once he finishes his education he will get a good job and take care of his parents
They think daughters are “paraya dhan” (someone else’s wealth as they marry and go to their husband’s home) and so don’t bother too much about her education
We don’t do much work in the fields
We don’t have any land; so there is no agricultural activity that we learn
We have too much to study; so there is no time to work in the fields
Today we all go to school and there is so much to study; so we don’t go our fields
Even boys don’t go the fields; they also study

Reasons for ending education
• Because of poverty
• Because girls get married early and so have to drop out of school
• If a girl’s body has matured then her parents get her married quickly
• I had enrolled in 11th but my parents got me married and I had to discontinue

Two most important reasons
• Because of poverty
• Because of early marriage
Girls end their education because:
Parents don’t have money
Parents are also always in a hurry to marry their daughters
I had not thought about anything special as such
I got married and there was no question of continuing with school after that
I wanted to study but my parents married me; I told my husband that I wanted to continue my studies but he did not let me
I cannot say what I would have wanted to do; I also got married and went to live with my husband and in- laws
We don’t study enough to think about doing something special with our lives
So there is no point in thinking about such things
Girls do “angna-ghar” work, i.e. all household chores
Boys work at the hotels
Some girls do stitching and such related work also
Boys also work in the fields
In some cases girls go to the fields for sorting grains
Boys also train as “raj mistry” i.e. master carpenter
Some also engage in harvesting in the fields
Apart from labour work, men should think about starting their own business
Men should think about doing something on their own for example setting up a coaching centre
But they mostly always engage in agriculture, that should not be the case
We girls never finish our education; what can we do
We only do household chores

We use machine for sowing (zero tiller) wheat seeds; sometimes we also sow manually
Tractor is used for ploughing; machine for sowing
“Honda” machine is used for irrigating the fields
There are a lot of pesticides used; don’t remember their names
There is both manual as well as machine work done in the fields
Harvesting is usually done by hand; sometimes by machine too
Sorting is usually done with a thresher
We use a pesticide called “thamus”
Hybrid seeds are also used
Weeding is done with the help of a weeder
For girls/women
Sowing with zero tiller
Sowing was earlier done by women
Weeder for wedding

For boys/men
Irrigating with the help of “honda” machine
Irrigating with the help of machine is faster
Sowing wheat with zero tiller
Makes it faster and less labour cost
We do have the same opportunities as the men but we are not able to do the same things
Yes, we women also learn to operate the machines; we learn everything
We are equal to men; if we want we can also learn all work related to agriculture
Men and women have equal rights to learn and do whatever farming related work they want to do
Module 2.  Gender norms, livelihoods, and family formation (1 ½ hours)

Important wheat innovation for [sex of FGD] Now
• Tractor for ploughing
• Zero tiller for sowing and giving fertilizers both
• “Honda” machine for irrigation
• Harvester
• Thresher for sorting
• Weeder
• Note: Harvester, thresher and weeder are important innovations for women

Important wheat innovation for [sex of FGD] 10 years ago
• Don’t know about innovations but most agricultural work was done manually
• Bulls and “fawda” were used for field preparation
• Sowing, putting fertilizers were done manually
• Water from rivers and lakes was used for irrigation
• Simple tools were (khurpi) used for weeding and harvesting
• Sorting was done by hands
• Cow dung was used as fertilizer
• Note: women did sowing, harvesting and sorting by hand, field preparation was always done by men since it required lot of physical labour
Till 10 years back all wheat farming was done manually
Bullocks and “fawda” were used for field preparation
We used water from rivers and lakes to irrigate our fields
Harvesting and sorting were done manually
Today tractor is used for ploughing
Before weeding was also done manually
The only manure used before was cow-dung
No one had any money before
There was no awareness before; now people are studying so they are more aware
People are also coming to our village to tell us about new machines which can be used in farming
It is because people are more educated now that they know about scientific inventions
After all weren’t these inventions done by very educated people
Some people have the money to be able to buy these machines; they then rent it to the smaller farmers, not everybody has money
Government also sometimes gives subsidies to buy these machines
Why will people not use machines? Is saves time and is easier
Women generally do the sowing.
Hand work are done by women mostly.
Machines are generally driven by men. Why? Because they are men and they go to the meetings where information about machines are generally shared.
Look, selling is not easy for anyone
Transport is a big problem; we carry our produce to the market on a cycle and if it doesn’t sell then we have to bring it back home on the cycle
If we use the public transport like auto then it becomes very expensive for us
Women also face the same problems
We cut, sort, weigh and then tie our yield in separate piles
We carry these sacks of our stuff to the market on our heads
Women also face security issues like eve teasing and men misbehaving with them
If our yield is not good then it doesn’t sell
Some people in the community tend to malign the character of women who go to sell on their own
Each family mostly has a single plot and yes women work on their husbands’ plots; it is the family plot actually
Women mostly do harvesting and sorting
Everybody is told about who will do what work
People sit and discuss division of work amongst them
All members of the family sit together and responsibilities are distributed; elders explain to the younger generation about how sowing and other work should be done
Sometime people from a few families who do farming sit together and decide on such issues
Big farmers have a lot of land and they usually get labour from within as well as outside to work on their land
Smaller farmers have little land and so you can say it is a single plot for the whole family
Small farmers work on bigger famers’ lands or sometimes lease land from them
Some households have kitchen gardens in their backyards where they grow vegetables; women take care of these kitchen gardens
Not applicable as couples don’t have separate plots
No women in our village owns her own plot; they work on their husbands’ plots
Women go to their field 5-6 times, they do sowing, harvesting, sorting everything
She would first consult her husband
She may also consult people who have such information
But it is important that she ask her husband
She may ask the concerned shopkeeper also (one who sells seeds)
Yes, men will also consult their wives; after all farming is all about taking different decisions and it is important to consult their spouse
He will not have any issue about her joining a group
Women work together in any case in the farm
It will be difficult for him to agree to his wife going out to sell
He will worry about what others will think about him if his wife goes out to sell
He will be scared that people will talk ill about his wife
Yes, village people will bad mouth his wife
Yes, Adam will still ask Ana for help since he thinks that the work on his plot is more important
Husband always thinks his work is more important than his wife’s
Sometimes some husbands who are educated may understand that their wives are also working hard and getting tired; so may not ask for their help
Many people will say that she has a bad character
Generally people will comment that the man of the house is sitting idle at home while his wife is going out to earn money
Some will comment that wife has more control at home than her husband; some may say such a husband is useless
Some villagers will appreciate that she is trying to help her family financially by working while also fulfilling her household obligations
Yes, some people may praise her
People will think bad about him and say that he sends his wife to work while he himself stays at home

People will ask him to go out and work and let his wife stay indoors
Some people will say that he is lucky because his wife is taking care of his wife and also supporting the family income by earning
If his wife is successful then he will be very happy since now there is more money for household expenses
He may even encourage her if she is doing well financially
Why not; after all she is doing all the household work and also earning; this is bonus
Who doesn’t like more money
Everybody here needs money
It is about man and woman doing all household work together
Equality means both should work together
They should not fight
Both should get the same education
Gender equality is good; today there is more gender equality as compared to before; there is more equality in education as well as in general outlook towards women; it was not so before
Today some of us can give our opinion about our marriage also
Yes, wife can also take such decisions; if she can work then she has the right to decide as well
They will take joint decision; they will keep 6-7 sacks for home consumption and sell the rest
Women know more about household needs, so she should decide how much to keep for home consumption
But her husband needs to agree to her
They will decide together
David will go to sell; his wife cannot go to the market
The village doesn’t look kindly upon woman who go out to sell; she is almost always mocked
Village women don’t go to the market

Yes, David will agree to her
